To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the uptake of 1) ursodeoxychoic acid, 2) cholic acid, and 3) taurocholic acids in the isolated hepatocytes is sodium dependent.
the uptake of UDAC in isolated hepatocytes is saturable and is dependent on Na+, and that the uptake of cholic and taurocholic acids in isolated hamster cells is saturable and Na+ dependent.
the uptake of UD CA in the hepatocyte is sodium dependent and that it is competitively inhibited by taurocholate and cholate.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the uptake of UD in the liver.
the mechanism by which sodium is involved in the uptake of bile acids.
the role of sodium in UDCA uptake by hepatocytes and with the possible role of a carrier system in UDCA transport across the cell membrane.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the uptake of UD CA in isolated hamster liver cells is a complex process involving both sodium‐dependent and sodium‐independent pathways.
the uptake of UDAC into isolated hepatocytes involves a sodium‐dependent, ouabian, amiloride and DIDS‐inhibited transport system.
the hepatocytal uptake of UDCA is a sodium‐dependent process that is mediated by a transporter with a low affinity (Km) for UDCA and is inhibited by both bile acids and stilbenes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
UDCA uptake in hamster hepatocyte is a sodium‐dependent process.
the sodium‐dependent transporter is the major pathway of hepatocellular uptake for both cholic acid and ursodeoxycolic acid.
the sodium‐dependent transport system is the major mechanism by which UDCA is taken up by the hepatocytes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
sodium‐dependent uptake plays a role in the hepatocellular transport of UDCA.

UDCA uptake in the hepatocytes is a sodium-dependent process and that this sodium dependence can be inhibited by amiloride, monensin and DIDS, which are known to inhibit sodium-dependent processes in other cells.
the uptake of 4‐keto bile acid is sodium‐dependent, which is different from the uptake of other bile acids.
